import pytest
from target import url_basename

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # simple single‑segment paths
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/foo/", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo?bar=1", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo#section", "foo"),
        # protocol‑relative URL
        ("//example.com/foo", "foo"),
        # no path after domain
        ("http://example.com/", ""),
        ("http://example.com", ""),
        # empty input
        ("", ""),
        # non‑matching strings
        ("example.com/foo", ""),
        # multiple path segments – old behaviour returns the last segment
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c", "c"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two/three/four", "four"),
        # trailing slash after last segment
        ("http://example.com/one/two/", "two"),
        # query or fragment after last segment
        ("http://example.com/one/two?x=1", "two"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two#frag", "two"),
        # path segment containing characters that are not allowed in the basename
        ("http://example.com/one/two?bad", "two"),
        ("http://example.com/one/two#bad", "two"),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_returns_expected_basename(url, expected):
    result = url_basename(url)
    assert isinstance(result, str)
    assert result == expected


def test_url_basename_unicode_handling():
    # Unicode characters in the path should be preserved
    url = "http://example.com/路径/文件名"
    assert url_basename(url) == "文件名"


def test_url_basename_edge_cases():
    # Very long path
    long_path = "/".join([f"segment{i}" for i in range(1000)])
    url = f"http://example.com/{long_path}"
    # Old implementation would return the last segment
    assert url_basename(url) == "segment999"

    # Path consisting only of slashes
    assert url_basename("http://example.com////") == ""

    # Path with empty segment before the basename
    assert url_basename("http://example.com//foo") == "foo"

    # Path with dot segments
    assert url_basename("http://example.com/./foo/..") == ".."
